dimensions.description: 1:8 museum model; overall including base 600 × 1040 × 350 mm. These are not locomotive-only dimensions and must not be imported as HO bounds.

observations: Record identifies wood, metal, brass, paint and paper: miniature craft uses distinct material layers, not one metal shader.
limitations: Early 2-2-0 engine is not the proposed fictional 0-6-0 tank engine. It informs model craftsmanship only, not exact silhouette or valve gear.
Museum dimensions include a base; photographic exposure does not establish PBR values.
references.decision: accepted for bounded research, not copied geometry or production art approval

references.title: National Railway Museum Locomotion report, part 2, printed pages 149–151
references.creator: National Railway Museum / Science Museum Group, report publisher; individual figure credits remain with the source
references.rightsHolder: Science Museum Group and credited contributors; image-specific rights not established
references.inspection: Report text describing bearings and crankpins read; PDF figures not downloaded into the repository.
references.rights: No commercial redistribution licence verified for report figures. All figure/text reproduction excluded.
references.attribution: National Railway Museum, Locomotion report part 2, section on coupling rods and crankpins; link only.

dimensions.description: The report contains measured historic components. None are dimensions for our fictional engine; author axle, crank radius and linkage lengths explicitly.

observations: Running gear needs distinguishable bearings, crankpins and rod ends, with attached pivots rather than a floating decorative bar.
limitations: Locomotion's historic mechanism is not a modern tank-engine valve-gear template.
Static documentation cannot approve our animation; forward/reverse motion and collision tests remain mandatory.
references.decision: accepted for mechanical vocabulary only; do not transplant historic mechanism
